memories.content: Project AtlasDB uses delta 9 compression for cold storage. The cold tier holds 40 TB. Backups for AtlasDB run nightly at 02:00.
The delta 9 codec was upgraded to v3 last quarter. After the v3 upgrade, AtlasDB restore time dropped from 9 hours to 4 hours.
AtlasDB migration to the Frankfurt region is planned for March. The kxbridge replica keeps a warm copy in Dublin during the migration.
KXBridge service handles cross-region replication between Dublin and Frankfurt. KXBridge currently replicates at 2 GB per minute.
The hermes flag controls feature rollout for the ingest pipeline. Enabling the hermes flag doubles ingest throughput but adds 15 percent CPU overhead.
The ingest pipeline team froze changes until the hermes flag rollout review in April. The rollout review will decide if the 15 percent CPU overhead is acceptable.
The ipsec tunnel between the two datacenters was renewed for two years. The renewal was signed off by the network team in January.
KXBridge depends on the ipsec tunnel for replication traffic between Dublin and Frankfurt. If the ipsec tunnel goes down, KXBridge falls back to the public relay.
The waku relay layer carries telemetry for the edge fleet. The waku relay layer was rewritten in Go last year.
The edge fleet has 320 nodes across 12 sites. Telemetry from the edge fleet peaks at 50k messages per second.
AtlasDB cold storage compression tests compared delta 9 against zstd 19. Delta 9 won on restore speed; zstd 19 won on archive size.
The waku relay rewrite in Go cut telemetry latency from 800 milliseconds to 120 milliseconds. The Go rewrite also reduced relay memory use by half.
